compatibility_badge: PCB Layout Change Required (Pinout or Package Mismatch)

pin_diff.note: PINOUT CONFLICT on Pin 1: TPS61200DRCR assigns VAUX (BYPASS) whereas TPS63001DRCR assigns VOUT (VOUT) — direct drop-in risks rail short or IC destruction.
PINOUT CONFLICT on Pin 2: TPS61200DRCR assigns VOUT (VOUT) whereas TPS63001DRCR assigns L2 (SW) — direct drop-in risks rail short or IC destruction.
PINOUT CONFLICT on Pin 3: TPS61200DRCR assigns L (SW) whereas TPS63001DRCR assigns PGND (GND) — direct drop-in risks rail short or IC destruction.
PINOUT CONFLICT on Pin 4: TPS61200DRCR assigns PGND (GND) whereas TPS63001DRCR assigns L1 (SW) — direct drop-in risks rail short or IC destruction.
PINOUT CONFLICT on Pin 7: TPS61200DRCR assigns UVLO (OTHER) whereas TPS63001DRCR assigns PS/SYNC (PS) — direct drop-in risks rail short or IC destruction.
PINOUT CONFLICT on Pin 8: TPS61200DRCR assigns PS (PS) whereas TPS63001DRCR assigns VINA (VIN) — direct drop-in risks rail short or IC destruction.
Feedback network difference: one device has fixed internal divider while the other requires external R1/R2 feedback resistors (PCB divider footprint change).

parameter_matrix.note: Synchronous rectification eliminates external Schottky diode loss and PCB area.
Compact WSON/VSON/SOT-563 packages demand tight hot-loop layout and thermal vias.
A part wins only if its operating Vin range strictly encompasses the counterpart on both ends.
Provides transient overshoot margin above nominal DC supply bus.
Fixed-output variants save divider BOM; adjustable parts allow arbitrary rail tuning up to switch BVdss limits.
For boost/switch-limited converters, usable Iout ≈ Isw × (Vin / Vout) × η minus half ripple ΔIL/2.
Dominates light-load efficiency and standby battery runtime.
Higher fsw shrinks inductor footprint; lower fsw reduces switching losses & high-band EMI.
Check datasheet efficiency curve at your exact Vin/Vout/Iout operating point.
Ensure inductor Isat exceeds worst-case peak switch current by >= 20–30%.
Any Vref discrepancy requires recalculating feedback divider R1/R2.
Lower θJA improves continuous load thermal headroom on compact 2-layer PCBs.

swap_risks: CRITICAL PINOUT CONFLICT: Incompatible pin assignments on Pin 1 (BYPASS vs VOUT), Pin 2 (VOUT vs SW), Pin 3 (SW vs GND), Pin 4 (GND vs SW), Pin 7 (OTHER vs PS), Pin 8 (PS vs VIN). Soldering TPS63001DRCR onto a TPS61200DRCR footprint (or vice versa) without rerouting copper can short VIN/VOUT/GND and permanently damage the board.

CRITICAL TOPOLOGY DIFFERENCE: TPS61200DRCR is a boost converter whereas TPS63001DRCR is a buck-boost converter; power-stage architecture, inductor placement, and startup behavior differ fundamentally — this is a power-path redesign, not a component swap.

CRITICAL FEEDBACK LAYOUT DIFFERENCE: One converter is fixed-output while the other is adjustable; adding or removing the external R1/R2 feedback divider and feedforward capacitor requires a PCB layout change.

CAUTION CURRENT RATING BASIS: TPS61200DRCR specifies 1350 mA (switch current limit Isw, p.6) vs TPS63001DRCR 1200 mA (continuous Iout, p.1). Remember boost/switch-limited Iout,max is strictly less than Isw due to duty-cycle and inductor ripple scaling.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: TPS63001DRCR requires Vin,min >= 1.8 V (p.4) vs 0.3 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.
engineering_verdict: TPS61200DRCR (Texas Instruments, VSON-10) and TPS63001DRCR (Texas Instruments, VSON-10) are NOT drop-in interchangeable (Level 3 PCB Layout / Circuit Change Required) due to pinout mismatch on Pin 1 (BYPASS vs VOUT), Pin 2 (VOUT vs SW), Pin 3 (SW vs GND), Pin 4 (GND vs SW), Pin 7 (OTHER vs PS), Pin 8 (PS vs VIN); DC-DC topology mismatch (boost vs buck-boost); fixed vs adjustable output feedback footprint mismatch (R1/R2 divider). Specific pin conflicts: Pin 1 (BYPASS vs VOUT), Pin 2 (VOUT vs SW), Pin 3 (SW vs GND), Pin 4 (GND vs SW). Power-stage deltas: boost (sync) vs buck-boost (sync), switching frequency 1450 kHz (p.6) vs 1500 kHz (p.5) (1x ratio), typical inductor 2.2 µH (p.15) vs 2.2 µH (p.1), output mode adjustable vs fixed, and package θJA 41.2 vs 46.8 °C/W. Primary bench gotchas to watch: TPS61200DRCR "Inverted PS Polarity (Fixed in Rev D) & Mandatory UVLO-to-VAUX / VAUX-Snubber Connections" (p.4) and TPS63001DRCR "Pin 10 (FB) MUST Be Connected Directly to VOUT on Fixed 3.3 V TPS63001" (p.3). BOM decision: Choose TPS61200DRCR when your power stage requires a boost topology; choose TPS63001DRCR when your power stage requires a buck-boost topology. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.4 vs TOP_VIEW p.3) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
